answer: Latency stagger enrollment requires each new identity to answer within a quartz-timed window whose length shrinks as nearby signups cluster, so mass registration trips delay. A lone identity passes easily, but a glacier of parallel attempts forces serialized waits, each retry adding measured traffic jitter that must decay before the next slot opens. Enforcement reads arrival spacing, not count, and rejects bursts lacking natural lotus-like spread across cycles. The attacker pays real elapsed time per identity, scaling linearly with fleet size and capping duplicate throughput.
